summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease status post kidney transplant, cirrhosis, gastroparesis, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for nausea, dark emesis, and crampy abdominal pain following minimal alcohol intake on Father's Day. Initial evaluation showed stable vital signs, mild lab abnormalities including thrombocytopenia and elevated lactate, and imaging that ruled out serious complications such as pneumomediastinum or bowel obstruction. Ultrasounds of the liver and renal transplants showed chronic but stable findings, with no signs of acute rejection or portal thrombosis. A recent endoscopy revealed gastroparesis without varices or ulcers. Gastroenterology consultation concluded no active bleeding, attributing the dark emesis to likely mild upper GI irritation. The patient improved with supportive care, including IV fluids, antiemetics, and proton-pump inhibition. He gradually resumed oral intake, remained hemodynamically stable, and was discharged home after two days with a course of ciprofloxacin, medication reconciliation, and follow-up plans.
